_: SINGLE NORMATIVE SOURCE for the speech-risk word list. Read by scripts/englyn-check.mjs AND by englyn/testing/harness/scan_text_transform_speech.py. Do NOT copy these values into either file: five instances of the copied-contract defect were found on 2026-08-18, the last two by no instrument at all, because documents quoted an enum they did not import.
_defect: A CSS text-transform uppercases text, WebKit hands the TRANSFORMED string to the accessibility tree, and a screen reader reads a short word as an initialism. 'What this buys us' is spoken 'What this buys U-S'.
_observed_note: Heard 2026-08-17, VoiceOver + Safari + WebKit, first agent-driven capture. axe/html-validate/englyn-check were all green at the time.
_likely_note: Established abbreviations of the same shape. Not individually heard.
_excluded_note: Common English words first, abbreviations second. Flagging them would fire on nearly every sentence and train everyone to ignore this check. Padding a criterion until it catches everything is how a check stops meaning anything.
_correctly_spelled_note: Words whose SPELLED form is the intended pronunciation, so uppercasing them is not a defect. Ruled by Micah 2026-08-19: 'ai' should be 'A-I'. The tag 'AI at work' spoken 'A-I at work' is CORRECT. Listed rather than silently dropped, because the next person to read this list will wonder why an obvious initialism is absent -- and because a risk list that flags a correct pronunciation trains people to ignore it.
